concepts.name: Cargo project workflow
concepts.summary: Create, build, run and check a Rust project with Cargo and explain what Cargo.toml and the src directory hold.

concepts.name: Immutable bindings and mutability
concepts.summary: Explain that variables are immutable by default and use mut to allow reassignment.

concepts.name: Scalar and compound types
concepts.summary: Recall integer, float, bool and char types plus tuples and fixed-size arrays, and how Rust infers types.

concepts.name: Functions and expressions
concepts.summary: Write functions with typed parameters and return values and explain that the last expression without a semicolon is returned.

concepts.name: Control flow constructs
concepts.summary: Use if as an expression and choose between loop, while and for over ranges.

concepts.name: Ownership and move semantics
concepts.summary: State the rules that each value has one owner, ownership moves on assignment, and the value is dropped when the owner goes out of scope.

concepts.name: String and &str
concepts.summary: Distinguish the owned, growable String from the borrowed string slice &str.

misconceptions.text: Assigning a String to another variable copies it so both remain usable.
A semicolon at the end of the last line of a function makes no difference to what it returns.
Variables in Rust are mutable like in most languages and mut is only a hint.

concepts.name: Shared and mutable references
concepts.summary: Borrow values with & and &mut and apply the rule of many readers or one writer.

concepts.name: Structs and impl blocks
concepts.summary: Define structs and implement methods and associated functions taking self, &self or &mut self.

concepts.name: Enums and pattern matching
concepts.summary: Model variants with data in enums and handle them exhaustively with match and if let.

concepts.name: Option and Result basics
concepts.summary: Represent absence and failure with Option and Result and unpack them with match, unwrap_or and the ? operator.

concepts.name: Vec and HashMap collections
concepts.summary: Store, iterate and update data in Vec and HashMap while respecting ownership of the elements.

concepts.name: Slices
concepts.summary: Borrow a contiguous part of a collection or string as a slice without copying.

concepts.name: Modules and visibility
concepts.summary: Organise code into modules, control visibility with pub and bring items into scope with use.

concepts.name: Copy versus Clone
concepts.summary: Explain which types are copied implicitly and when an explicit clone is needed.

misconceptions.text: A reference works like a C pointer, so any number of mutable references to the same value may exist at once.
Calling unwrap is the normal way to handle an Option or Result.
Cloning a value is free, so it is the right fix for every borrow checker error.

concepts.name: Lifetime annotations
concepts.summary: Annotate functions and structs with lifetime parameters to relate the validity of references and apply elision rules.

concepts.name: Traits and implementations
concepts.summary: Define traits with required and default methods and implement them for your own types.

concepts.name: Generics with trait bounds
concepts.summary: Write generic functions and types constrained by trait bounds and analyse how they compile to specialised code.

concepts.name: Custom error types
concepts.summary: Design error enums implementing Display and Error with From conversions so the ? operator propagates them.

concepts.name: Iterators and closures
concepts.summary: Compose map, filter and collect pipelines and analyse how closures capture their environment.

concepts.name: Smart pointers Box and Rc
concepts.summary: Choose Box for heap allocation and recursive types and Rc for shared ownership within a single thread.

concepts.name: Unit and integration tests
concepts.summary: Write unit tests in modules and integration tests in the tests directory and run them with cargo test.

concepts.name: Cargo dependencies and features
concepts.summary: Add crates, manage Cargo.lock and workspaces and toggle optional features.

misconceptions.text: Lifetime annotations extend how long a value lives.
Generics in Rust are resolved at runtime like virtual dispatch, so they cost performance.
Iterator adapters like map do work immediately and allocate a new collection at each step.

concepts.name: Interior mutability patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse when Cell and RefCell move borrow checking to runtime and combine them with Rc safely.

concepts.name: Threads and message passing
concepts.summary: Spawn threads, move data into them and coordinate with channels.

concepts.name: Shared state with Arc and Mutex
concepts.summary: Share mutable state across threads with Arc and Mutex and reason about contention and deadlock.

concepts.name: Send and Sync marker traits
concepts.summary: Explain how Send and Sync encode thread-safety at compile time and determine which types satisfy them.

concepts.name: Trait objects and dynamic dispatch
concepts.summary: Evaluate trait objects against generics in terms of flexibility, performance and object-safety limits.

concepts.name: Async and await model
concepts.summary: Explain how futures are polled by a runtime and decide when async fits I/O-bound services.

concepts.name: Advanced trait features
concepts.summary: Use associated types, default generic parameters, supertraits and the orphan rule to design coherent APIs.

concepts.name: Profiling and release optimisation
concepts.summary: Measure performance with release builds and benchmarks and judge which optimisations are justified.

misconceptions.text: Rust's type system prevents all concurrency bugs, including deadlocks and logic races.
RefCell bypasses the borrow rules so they no longer apply.
Async code runs on multiple threads automatically and is always faster than threads.

concepts.name: Unsafe Rust and invariants
concepts.summary: Judge when unsafe is justified and state the invariants a safe wrapper must uphold to avoid undefined behaviour.

concepts.name: Foreign function interface
concepts.summary: Evaluate and build safe bindings to C libraries handling layout, ownership and error boundaries.

concepts.name: Declarative and procedural macros
concepts.summary: Create macros that remove boilerplate while keeping errors clear and hygiene intact.

concepts.name: Library API design
concepts.summary: Design public crate APIs with ergonomic types, stable semver guarantees and sensible error and trait choices.

concepts.name: Pin and self-referential futures
concepts.summary: Evaluate why pinning is needed for async state machines and apply it correctly in custom futures.

concepts.name: Memory model and atomics
concepts.summary: Choose atomic memory orderings and judge whether lock-free designs are worth their complexity.

concepts.name: Verifying unsafe code
concepts.summary: Assess the soundness of unsafe code with Miri, fuzzing and property tests.

concepts.name: Embedded and no_std design
concepts.summary: Architect libraries that work without the standard library, relying on core and optional alloc.

misconceptions.text: Unsafe code turns off the borrow checker and all of Rust's safety rules inside the block.
If code with unsafe compiles and passes tests, it is sound.
Relaxed atomic ordering is always safe and fastest, so it can be used everywhere.
